chunks: From him, from Faḍālah, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought a slave-girl who had not yet menstruated and had stolen, so he flogged her with lashes and did not amputate her.

key_terms.أَسْوَاطًا: lashes or strokes with a whip
key_terms.بِجَارِيَةٍ: a slave-girl brought before the authority
key_terms.فَضَرَبَهَا: he struck her as a disciplinary punishment
key_terms.لَمْ تَحِضْ: she had not yet menstruated, indicating prepubescence
key_terms.وَلَمْ يَقْطَعْهَا: he did not amputate her hand

ai.seo_question: What was the ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام for a girl who had not yet menstruated if she stole?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a judicial ruling from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام regarding a prepubescent slave-girl who committed theft. It indicates that the ḥadd of amputation was not applied to her, and that she was instead disciplined with lashes.
